correctness.rationale: For the canonical conic \(C_0=[a:b:c:c:a:b:b:c:a]\) with \(b^2+c^2=2a^2\), the sign subgroup has stabilizer \(2^3/2=4\), hence orbit 64; a square reflection exchanges the cyclic and anticyclic families, so the full 2048-element group has one orbit of 128 conics and stabilizer 16. The indicated Jacobian minor is \(-6^6a^2b^2c^2\), excluding singularities when \(abc\ne0\). The three zero-coordinate cuts give two points each; their published square patterns identify four as type \(p_1\) and two as type \(p_3\). Triviality gives exactly four projective sign classes. Double counting then forces the incidence multiplicities 2, 4, 0, 4. All finite identities are replayed from the packaged verifier.

value.rationale: The initiating paper explicitly asks whether its 128 known conics exhaust all conics. Before tackling that classification, the automorphism orbit and incidence design of the known candidate set are natural structural data: they identify a single homogeneous conic family, its stabilizer, and the exact way it meets the distinguished finite loci of the surface. These constraints are useful for organizing any Hilbert- or Fano-scheme analysis of additional conics and are not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere recomputation of a published table.
